subject: Post-demo: buying landscape, MAP proposal & procurement asks
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@clearmap.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed MAP & next steps

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for a great demo today. High-level recap and proposed next steps below so we all have the same frame. I’ll drop a draft MAP to the Drive after this email for you and Rachel to review.

Quick recap (from our notes):
- Use case: automated map-matching and address-intelligence to improve routing and data quality for ClearMap's delivery ops.
- Success signals: 5% reduction in avg. route deviation, 98% address match rate, integration with existing S3 ingestion pipeline.
- Technical fit: Redwood model selection + prefix caching looks to satisfy latency and batch throughput targets discussed.

Key buying stakeholders (please confirm or correct):
- Economic buyer: Rachel Turner (CFO) — budget ownder (you indicated she signs off on platform costs)
- Procurement/legal: procurement@clearmap.ai (procurement intake)
- Security contact: security@clearmap.ai — expects SOC2 and data flow diagram
- Technical champion: Liam O'Neil (you) — owning POC success criteria and ops requirements

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) — top-level milestones:
1) Technical workshop & POC scope (this week — goal: finalize scope and test dataset)
2) Security review & evidence exchange (SOC2 summary + data processing notes)
3) Commercial proposal and T&Cs (pricing band for 3-month POC + enterprise SKU for production)
4) POC kickoff and run (2–4 weeks)
5) Exec review and procurement signoff (decision gate)

Asks / next steps:
- Liam: can you confirm Rachel is the economic approver and provide her preferred cadence for a brief buy-in call?
- Liam / Procurement: please confirm procurement email and any procurement template/PO terms you require.
- ClearMap security: what evidence artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption at rest, retention policy) do you typically need up front?

Attachments I’ll add to the thread: a one-sheet MAP stub, SOC2 summary from Redwood, and a POC scope doc.

Proposed times for the technical workshop: Thu 7/19 10:00–11:00 AM PT or Fri 7/20 9:00–10:00 AM PT — pick one and I’ll send calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

—
Irene Choi
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0118
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed MAP & next steps

Irene — thanks for the clear recap and props to the team for a clean demo. Confirming a few items from our side:

- Rachel Turner is the economic approver and will want a short 20-min overview focused on ROI (cost per route improvement and ops savings). I’ll introduce you by email once you share the MAP doc.
- Procurement intake is procurement@clearmap.ai — they prefer to see a quote + standard SOW and initiate their redline process. PO terms are typical net-30.
- Security will want Greenwood's SOC2 type II report (or summary) and a data flow diagram showing where tokens/data live. They asked specifically about retention and whether any PII leaves our VPC.

Timeline constraints: Quarter close is Aug 25 — Rachel wants a decision by Sep 15 if we’re in the running. So ideal: POC kickoff in early Aug, 3–4 week run, then exec review.

I can do the tech workshop Fri 7/20 9–10 AM PT. Please send invite.

—
Liam O'Neil
Director, Platform + Integrations, ClearMap AI
liam.oneil@clearmap.ai | (617) 555-0199

Thanks — adding a couple of technical detail points we should have ready for the workshop and include in the MAP doc:

- Ingest: preferred sample dataset size? Recommend 50k historical routes (anonymized) to exercise latency and cache behaviors.
- Auth & network: we support VPC peering or short-lived signed URLs; if ClearMap prefers S3 IAM role, we can provide a connector template.
- SOC2 summary: attaching the one-pager (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) and adding a short note on encryption (AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit).

I’ll create a technical checklist in the Drive and populate it before the workshop. Also prepared a POC runbook template that defines success criteria and observability checks.

Next steps for us:
- Irene: share MAP draft to Drive and intro to Rachel after Liam confirms.
- Aditya: finalize tech checklist + prepare test dataset guide.
- Monica: prepare commercial framework (3-month POC pricing + production estimate).

—
Aditya Rao
